title: Filtered colimit of injective sheaves is Cech-acyclic on a quasi-compact basis
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space whose quasi-compact opens form a basis and whose pairwise intersections of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, every two elements have a common upper bound), $(\mathcal I_i,\varphi_{i'i})_{i\le i'}$ a system of injective abelian sheaves on $X$ over $I$, and $\mathcal I=\varinjlim_i\mathcal I_i$ its colimit in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every quasi-compact open $U$ and every finite covering $\mathcal U=\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ of $U$ by quasi-compact opens with all finite intersections quasi-compact, the Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] satisfies $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for all $p>0$. Hence $H^q(U,\mathcal I)=0$ for $q>0$, where $H^q(U,-)=R^q\Gamma(U,-)$ is cohomology over the object $U$ of the open site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (for $U=X$ the cohomology of [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]).

proof.text: Fix a finite covering $\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ of a quasi-compact open $U$ by quasi-compact opens, with all finite intersections quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-directed-colimit-underlying-sets] (for the constant sheaf of rings $\mathbf Z$, whose modules are the abelian sheaves) the underlying sheaf of sets of $\mathcal I$, with the underlying maps of the colimit maps, is the colimit of the underlying sheaves of sets of the $\mathcal I_i$ in sheaves of sets. For each iterated intersection $W=U_{t_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{t_p}$ occurring in the Cech terms, the finite coverings of $W$ by quasi-compact basis opens are cofinal among open coverings (refine an arbitrary covering pointwise by basis opens and choose a finite subcover by quasi-compactness of $W$), and their pairwise intersections are quasi-compact by hypothesis. Thus clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-directed-colimit-sections] gives that $\varinjlim_i\mathcal I_i(W)\to\mathcal I(W)$ is bijective, hence an isomorphism of abelian groups. For $p\ge0$ the $p$-th Cech term is the finite product $\prod_{\mathbf t\in T^{p+1}}\mathcal I(U_{\mathbf t})$; a directed colimit of abelian groups commutes with finite products (represent a tuple at finitely many stages and pass to a common upper bound), so $\varinjlim_i\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ is an isomorphism. These isomorphisms commute with the alternating restriction differentials by naturality of restriction, hence identify $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ with $\varinjlim_i\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)$.

Each $\mathcal I_i$ is injective, so $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)$ is exact in every positive degree by [lem-weil-pbc-site-injective-cech-acyclic]. A directed set is a filtered category, so by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] the colimit complex is exact in every positive degree as well. By Step 1, $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for $p>0$.

Let $\mathcal B$ be the set of quasi-compact opens of $X$ and $\mathrm{Cov}$ the set of finite coverings of a member of $\mathcal B$ by members of $\mathcal B$ whose finite intersections are quasi-compact. Condition (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] holds since fibre products in the open site are intersections, which lie in $\mathcal B$ by induction on the number of factors. Condition (2): every open covering of $U\in\mathcal B$ is refined by a member of $\mathrm{Cov}$ (refine pointwise by basis opens and take a finite subcover). Step 2 gives condition (3). The criterion yields $H^q(U,\mathcal I)=0$ for every $q>0$ and $U\in\mathcal B$, with $H^q(U,-)=R^q\Gamma(U,-)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].
